messages:
maya-ml: Heads up — ran AWQ quantization bakeoff for Mistral-3 on the TRTLLM runtime and hit weird scheduling stalls under load. latency spikes + occasional OOM-ish traces, not reproducing on vLLM path. :thinking:
ev an-runtime: Can you paste the baseline numbers and the exact Triton/TRTLLM builds?
maya-ml: Baseline (fp16/trtllm 8f3b): 210 tps @ seq=1024 batch=4. AWQ-int8 candidate: 410 tps but tail latency spikes 300-800ms every few minutes. gptq-int8 on vLLM: 395 tps steady.
dmitri-devex: Do you see any cuMemAlloc failures in the logs? Those often correlate with fragmentation across kernels. Also which driver + CUDA?
maya-ml: CUDA 15.2, nvidia-driver 555.80, TRT-LLM plugin 0.9.1, triton-server 23.12. Logs show some alloc/backpressure, plus this stacktrace repeated:
```
# log snippet
E 03:41:12 kernel_launch: cudaErrorIllegalInstruction at inference_kernel.cu:432
W 03:41:12 memory: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (0x3e5)
I 03:41:12 fallback: scheduling stall detected, switching to fallback queue
```

annah: I ran a short repro with seq=2048 batch=2 on same hw and saw the stall happen only when continuous-batching enabled in TRTLLM (same model + awq). Turning off batching made it stable but performance dropped ~25%. :eyes:
ev an-runtime: That points to a kernel fusion / workspace sizing issue in TRTLLM for AWQ kernels. When continuous batching folds different request shapes it can change workspace needs mid-flight and cause transient allocation failures. Can you try setting TRTLLM_BATCHER_MAX_WORKSPACE=0 to force per-request workspaces?
maya-ml: Trying now. Also saw a strange regression in kv-cache hits: cache hit rate falls from ~98% to ~84% under AWQ under sustained traffic. Could be a threading race.
dmitri-devex: Please upload the small repro script to the infra bucket and include env + model config. Quick command we used to repro locally:
```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python perf_probe.py --model mistral-3-awq --seq 2048 --batch 2 --duration 600 
```
Include trtllm config fields: `continuous_batching: true`, `max_workspace_bytes: null` and plugin env.

infra-bot: pod/reproducer-ml-231 restarted by cron at 2026-03-20T09:12:33Z (reason: OOMKill), logs archived to s3://redwood-logs/eng-ml/1927654321/repro.tar.gz

annah: After forcing per-request workspace (TRTLLM_BATCHER_MAX_WORKSPACE=0) the stalls stopped in my run but throughput dropped to ~315 tps. Also accuracy delta: AWQ-int8 vs fp16 on our eval set dropped -1.2% R@1 on retrieval prompts compared to gptq-int8 (-0.4%). So AWQ still interesting for perf but larger quality variance.
ev an-runtime: For next steps: 1) get a minimal repro script and trtllm config, 2) bisect TRTLLM plugin between 0.9.0 and 0.9.1, 3) open issue with NVIDIA if kernel invalid-instruction persists, include the `kernel_launch` stack + coredump.
maya-ml: Filed internal issue INF-ML-4721 and added repro + s3 link. Also included perf table and eval delta. Can someone try a quick run with `TRTLLM_PERF_FORCE_FALLBACK=1` (forces slower but safer kernels) to see if that stabilizes without workspace hack?
dmitri-devex: Running now on p2.1 (same hw pool). Command: `kubectl exec -it repro -- /bin/bash -c "export TRTLLM_PERF_FORCE_FALLBACK=1; ./run_repro.sh"`

infra-bot: job/repro-run-1927654321 completed (exit 0). Artifacts: s3://redwood-logs/eng-ml/1927654321/forced-fallback.tar.gz

annah: Forced fallback run: 330 tps, stable. Tail latency median 45ms, p99 120ms. Accuracy same as previous AWQ run (-1.2). Conclusion: fallback avoids illegal instruction / allocation race but reduces perf.
ev an-runtime: Sounds like kernel selection issue in TRTLLM's AWQ path. If fallback is stable we can ship a runtime guard: detect illegal-instruction / repeated cuMemAlloc and flip to fallback kernel set per model. That keeps perf for well-behaved models and avoids downtime for noisy ones.
maya-ml: Agree. I'll add a canary rollout config to Redwood Optimize to try fallback for 10% of traffic and monitor token-cost delta + quality regressions. Putting this thread's artifacts in INF-ML-4721. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
